title: The King and Check
subtitle: One square at a time — and how to answer a check.
goals: Move the king one square in any direction
Escape check three ways: move, block, capture

steps.say: The king — the whole game in one piece. He moves just one square in any direction, and he can never step onto a square an enemy attacks. When the king is attacked, it's called CHECK, and you must deal with it immediately.
Watch a check happen — and how the defender must respond.

autoMoves.say: Check! The rook attacks the king along the back rank. Black is not allowed to ignore this.
The king steps off the attacked line. Every check must be answered before anything else.

steps.prompt: You're in check! Your king can't move — block the attack instead.
hints: Three ways out of check: move the king, capture the attacker, or block the line. Here, moving and capturing are impossible.
Put a piece in the rook's path on the h-file. Two of your pieces can do it.

line.say: The rook slides across and shields the king. Block delivered!
The bishop tucks in front of the king. A perfect little shield!

steps.wrongSay: You're in check — only a move that stops the attack is legal. Put something between the rook and your king.
steps.successSay: Move, block, capture — you just used option two. Always check all three.

steps.prompt: The queen says check — but she came too close without backup. What now?
hints: Move, block, or capture. Look closely at the checking piece — is anyone protecting her?
The queen is right next to your king and completely undefended. Take her!

line.say: The king captures the queen! A check from an unprotected piece next to your king is just a gift.

steps.wrongSay: Only one legal move exists here — the checking queen has no bodyguard...
steps.successSay: Never panic at a check. Sometimes the 'attacker' is the one in danger.

steps.prompt: Your turn to attack — give the black king a check!
hints: A check is any move that attacks the enemy king. Your rook has two ways to do it.
Line up with the king: same rank or same file.

line.say: Check! The rook owns the back rank and stares straight at the king.
Check! The rook takes the e-file — the king's own avenue.

steps.wrongSay: No check yet. Move the rook onto the king's rank or file.
steps.successSay: Checks force your opponent to react — they're the most forcing moves in chess.

steps.prompt: Two checks are possible — but one loses a piece. Find the SAFE check!
hints: Before checking, ask: can the king (or anyone) just capture my piece?
The bishop check lands right next to the king. The rook check attacks from a safe distance.

line.say: Check from across the board — the king can't touch you. That's a quality check.

rejections.say: Check — but Kxf7! The king simply eats your undefended bishop. A check that loses material is usually a bad check.

steps.wrongSay: Look for a check the king cannot answer by capturing your piece.
steps.successSay: Checks are only good when they're safe or achieve something. You just learned that ahead of schedule.
